Originally established as a wholly owned subsidiary of [[ZTE]] in 2012, it became an independent company in 2015{{cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/enterprises/article/1819590/chinas-nubia-becomes-independent-brand-gain-traction-red-hot|title=China's Nubia becomes independent from ZTE to gain traction in smartphone market|date=10 June 2015|access-date=11 April 2018|work=South China Morning Post|location=Hong Kong}} and received a significant investment from [[Suning Holdings Group]] and [[Suning Commerce Group]] in 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.suning.cn/static///snsite/contentresource/2016-04-30/4a866977-bf23-4d98-b998-f479a0c0bae8.pdf|title=关于受让股权的关联交易公告|trans-title=Announcement on related-party transaction for buying equity stake in a company|date=30 April 2016|access-date=7 June 2016|publisher=Suning Commerce Group|language=Chinese}} ZTE reduced its stake in Nubia to 49.9% in 2017. Officially, this meant Nubia was no longer considered a subsidiary of ZTE, but rather an [[associate company]].[http://res.www.zte.com.cn/mediares/zte/Investor/20170727/E3.pdf Disposal of 10.1% of the equity interest in Nubia Technology Limited], ZTE Corporation, 27 July 2017, Retrieved on 8 April 2018 In February 2016 Nubia became a sponsor of [[Jiangsu Suning F.C.]] for a reported {{CNY|150 million}}.{{cite web|url=http://en.ytsports.cn/news-2164.html|title=Nubia to sponsor Jiangsu Suning FC for RMB150m|date=18 February 2016|access-date=11 April 2016|website=ytsports.cn}} The company hired footballer [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] to promote the mobile phone of the company in May 2016.{{cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/china-tech/article/2017252/ztes-nubia-aims-become-top-five-smartphone-brand-globally|title=ZTE's Nubia aims to become top five smartphone brand globally|date=7 September 2016|access-date=12 August 2017|work=South China Morning Post|location=Hong Kong}} In 2017, ''[[China Daily]]'' reported that Nubia would build a factory in [[Nanchang]], Jiangxi Province.{{cite news|url=http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/business/2017-08/09/content_30389845.htm|title=Smartphone maker Nubia plans plant in Jiangxi|date=9 August 2017|access-date=20 August 2017|work=China Daily}} In April 2018, Nubia Technology launched a gaming sub-brand, named [[REDMAGIC]] (红魔).{{cite news|url=https://www.theverge.com/circuitbreaker/2018/4/19/17257974/nubia-red-magic-smartphone-gaming-led-lights-zte-android|title=Nubia's Red Magic smartphone is designed for gaming, down to the glowing LEDs on the back|date=19 April 2018|access-date=15 April 2020|work=The Verge}} REDMAGIC announced its new 5G compatible device REDMAGIC 5G on 12 March 2020, in Shanghai. REDMAGIC is known for being the first smartphone brand to put [[Active cooling|cooling fans]] inside their phones.{{Cite web|title=Nubia Just Stuffed the First Active Fan Inside a Smartphone - ExtremeTech|url=https://www.extremetech.com/mobile/290683-nubia-just-stuffed-the-first-active-fan-inside-a-smartphone|access-date=2020-09-07|website=www.extremetech.com}}{{Cite web|last=Amadeo|first=Ron|date=2020-03-13|title=Red Magic 5G gaming smartphone has 144hz display, internal cooling fan|url=https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2020/03/red-magic-5g-gaming-smartphone-has-144hz-display-internal-cooling-fan/|access-date=2020-09-07|website=Ars Technica|language=en-us}} The company also unveiled a partnership with Chinese esport team [[Royal Never Give Up]], to further expand its brand among esport enthusiasts.{{Cite web |title=We're teaming up with Royal Never Give Up |url=https://eu.redmagic.gg/blogs/news/we-re-teaming-up-with-royal-never-give-up |access-date=2022-07-01 |website=RedMagic |date=29 December 2018 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=努比亚红魔Mars电竞手机RNG六周年纪念版明天发售：3299元 |url=https://news.mydrivers.com/1/610/610327.htm |access-date=2022-07-01 |website=快科技}} On 13 April 2020, the company unveiled a brand new logo as well as its new brand vision.{{Cite web|title=Nubia unveils new logo and brand vision as it expands product categories|url=https://www.gizmochina.com/2020/04/13/nubia-new-logo-brand-vision/|last=Jeet|date=2020-04-13|website=Gizmochina|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-10}} In March 2022, Nubia unveiled the first gaming phone featuring an under-display camera technology, the REDMAGIC 7 Pro.{{Cite web |title=The Nubia Red Magic 7 Pro packs an under-display camera, RGB lighting, and more |url=https://www.techspot.com/news/94176-nubia-red-magic-7-pro-packs-under-display.html |access-date=2022-07-01 |website=TechSpot |date=13 April 2022 |language=en-US}} In 2023, Nubia released the Red Magic 8S Pro, touted as the strongest gaming phone to date. In 2024, Nubia released the Red Magic 9S Pro+ with the highest [[AnTuTu|Antutu]] smartphone score to date.{{as of when|date=August 2026}}{{Cite web |title=标准版性能_手机性能排行榜_安兔兔跑分排行_安兔兔 |url=https://www.antutu.com/ranking/rank1.htm |access-date=2024-08-20 |website=www.antutu.com}} In July 2024, RedMagic announced its entry in the computer category with its first gaming laptop, the Titan 16 Pro,{{Cite web |last=Vlad |title=Red Magic Titan 16 Pro laptop launches with Intel Core i9 and RTX4060 or RTX4070 graphics |url=https://www.gsmarena.com/red_magic_titan_16_pro_laptop_launches_with_intel_core_i9_and_rtx4060_or_rtx4070_graphics-news-63562.php |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=GSMArena.com |language=en-US}} available in China and global markets, while in September, they launched their first gaming tablet, the Nova gaming pad.{{Cite web |last=Vasile |first=Cosmin |date=2024-09-05 |title=Meet the Red Magic Nova, Nubia's new gaming tablet |url=https://www.phonearena.com/news/red-magic-nova-gaming-tablet-official_id162264 |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=PhoneArena |language=en-US}}

The '''biology of trust''' is the study of [[Physiology|physiological]] mechanisms involved in mediating [[Trust (emotion)|trust]] in social attachments. It has been studied in terms of [[genetics]], [[endocrinology]] and [[neurobiology]].<ref name="riedl">{{cite journal|last1=Riedl|first1=Rene|last2=Javor|first2=Andrija|title=The Biology of Trust: Integrating Evidence From Genetics, Endocrinology, and Functional Brain Imaging|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/232431419|journal=[[Journal of Neuroscience, Psychology, and Economics]]|date=2011|volume=5|issue=2|page=63|doi=10.1037/a0026318}}</ref>

Trust is the intentional choice to believe the input of strangers because one believes they know the truth and have one's best interest at heart.<ref name=":3">{{Cite book|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK321980/|title=What Is Trust|last1=Sciences|first1=Roundtable on Public Interfaces of the Life|last2=Sciences|first2=Board on Life|last3=Studies|first3=Division on Earth and Life|last4=Education|first4=Board on Science|last5=Education|first5=Division of Behavioral and Social Sciences and|last6=The National Academies of Sciences|first6=Engineering|date=2015-09-23|publisher=National Academies Press (US)|language=en}}</ref> Trust is important in creating social attachments. 

Social bonds is a characteristic present in many mammals and other vertebrae species.<ref name=":22">{{Cite journal|last=Feldman|first=Ruth|title=The Neurobiology of Human Attachments|journal=Trends in Cognitive Sciences|volume=21|issue=2|pages=80–99|doi=10.1016/j.tics.2016.11.007|pmid=28041836|year=2017|s2cid=3651287}}</ref> However, there exists a paradox in the formation of social bonds in humans- while there are benefits, drawbacks, such as judgment, vulnerabilities to harmful physical and emotional hurt do exist.<ref name=":02">{{Cite book|title=Annual review of psychology. Volume 66, 2015|others=Fiske, Susan T.,, Schacter, Daniel L.,, Taylor, Shelley E.|isbn=9780824302665|location=Palo Alto, California|oclc=897575784|year = 1953}}</ref> And overarching all of this is [[Trust (emotion)|trust]], which is marked by the intentional choice to rely on another individual for an underlying purpose, despite drawbacks- a factor in social bonds with [[Biology|biological]] implications.<ref name=":3" />

'''Jacqueline Bishop''' is a writer, visual artist and photographer from Jamaica, who now lives in New York City, where she is a professor at the School of Liberal Studies at [[New York University]] (NYU).<ref name=HuffPost>[https://www.huffingtonpost.com/author/jacqueline-bishop Jacqueline Bishop profile] at ''HuffPost''.</ref> She is the founder of ''Calabash'', an online journal of Caribbean art and letters, housed at NYU,<ref>Xavier Murphy, [https://jamaicans.com/interview-with-jacqueline-bishop-founding-editor-o/ "Interview with Jacqueline Bishop, founding editor of Calabash: A Journal of Caribbean Arts & Letters"], Jamaicans.com.</ref> and also writes for the ''[[Huffington Post]]'' and the ''[[Jamaica Observer]]'' Arts Magazine. In 2016 her book ''The Gymnast and Other Positions'' won the nonfiction category of the [[OCM Bocas Prize for Caribbean Literature]].<ref>[http://www.peepaltreepress.com/blog/whappen/2016-ocm-bocas-prize-category-winners-announced "2016 OCM Bocas Prize category winners announced"], ''Wha'ppen?'' (Peepal Tree Press blog), 30 March 2016.</ref> She is a contributor to the 2019 anthology ''[[Daughters of Africa#New Daughters of Africa|New Daughters of Africa]]'', edited  by [[Margaret Busby]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.somersethouse.org.uk/whats-on/get-up-stand-up-now/margaret-busby-presents-new-daughters-africa|title=Margaret Busby Presents: NEW DAUGHTERS OF AFRICA – Part of GET UP, STAND UP NOW|publisher=[[Somerset House]]|date=9 September 2019|access-date=7 April 2021|archive-date=20 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210720215911/https://www.somersethouse.org.uk/whats-on/get-up-stand-up-now/margaret-busby-presents-new-daughters-africa|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''''Tumor Biology''''' (also '''''Tumour Biology''''') is a bimonthly [[peer-review]]ed [[open access]] [[medical journal]] covering clinical and experimental [[oncology]]. It was established in 1980 as '''''Oncodevelopmental Biology and Medicine''''', obtaining its current name in 1984. It is owned by the [[International Society of Oncology and BioMarkers]], of which it is the official journal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://us.sagepub.com/en-us/nam/tumor-biology/journal202707#aims-and-scope |title=Aims and Scope |website=Tumor Biology Website|date=28 September 2016 }}</ref><ref name=science>{{Cite web |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/china-cracks-down-after-investigation-finds-massive-peer-review-fraud |title=China cracks down after investigation finds massive peer-review fraud |last=Normile |first=Dennis |date=2017-07-31 |website=Science |language=en |access-date=2017-12-15}}</ref> Originally published by [[Karger Publishers]], it moved to [[Springer Science+Business Media]] beginning in 2010.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Stigbrand |first=Torgny |date=2017-01-01 |title=The rapidly changing landscape of scientific publishing |journal=Tumor Biology |language=en |volume=39 |issue=1 |article-number=1010428316687894 |doi=10.1177/1010428316687894 |pmid=28121285 |issn=1010-4283|doi-access=free }}</ref> In December 2016, the journal moved again, this time to [[SAGE Publications]].<ref name=science/> The [[editor-in-chief]] is Magdalena Chechlinska ([[Curie Institute, Warsaw]]). According to the ''[[Journal Citation Reports]]'', the journal has a 2016 [[impact factor]] of 3.650.<ref name=WoS>{{cite book |year=2017 |chapter=Tumor Biology |title=2016 Journal Citation Reports |publisher=[[Clarivate Analytics]] |edition=Science |series=[[Web of Science]]|title-link=Journal Citation Reports }}</ref>

[[image:Snyders_Dogs_fighting_demonstrating_Golden_Triangle_composition_method.jpg|right|thumb|300px|Example of Golden Triangle method on a painting. Compositional elements fall within the triangles.]]
The '''golden triangle''' is a rule of thumb in [[Composition (visual arts)|visual composition]] of photographs, paintings, and other visual art—especially those that contain elements with diagonal lines. The rule visualizes the frame divided into four triangles of two different sizes, by drawing one diagonal from one corner to another, and then two lines from the other corners, touching the first at 90-degree angles. There are a couple ways to apply this: 

1. Filling one of the triangles with the subject<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.crispphotoworks.com/photography-composition-the-golden-triangle-rule|title=Photography Composition the Golden Triangle Rule|access-date=2018-03-12}}</ref>

2. Placing the diagonal elements so that they run along two of the lines<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digital-photo-secrets.com/tip/3372/18-composition-rules-for-photos-that-shine/|title=18 Composition Rules for Photos that Shine|access-date=2018-03-12}}</ref>

{{Short description|Land divisions not interrupted by other land or water}}
[[File:Archipelago Sea and Aland.svg|thumb|[[Åland]], the autonomous [[Regions of Finland|region of Finland]], and the [[Islands of Turku|Turku archipelago]] belonging to the rest of Finland in the [[Archipelago Sea]].]]

'''Geographic contiguity''' is the characteristic in [[geography]] of political or geographical land divisions, as a group, not being interrupted by other land or water. Such divisions are referred to as being ''contiguous.'' In the [[United States]], for example, the "[[Contiguous United States|48 contiguous states]]" excludes [[Hawaii]] and [[Alaska]], which do not share borders with other [[U.S. state]]s.<ref>[https://wetlandsfws.er.usgs.gov/imf/sites/NWI_CONUS/CONUS_metadata/CONUS_Layers.html Wetlands Metadata for the Lower 48 States, US Fish and Wildlife Service] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071105143231/http://wetlandsfws.er.usgs.gov/imf/sites/NWI_CONUS/CONUS_metadata/CONUS_Layers.html |date=5 November 2007 }}</ref> Other examples of geographical contiguity might include the "contiguous [[European Union]]" excluding member states such as Ireland, Sweden, Finland (between [[Åland]] and [[Islands of Turku|Turku Archipelago]]), Malta and Cyprus (these being non-contiguous), or the "contiguous United Kingdom" referring to all parts of the country excepting [[Northern Ireland]] (it being geographically non-contiguous). Two or more contiguous [[Municipality|municipalities]] can be consolidated into one, or one municipality can consist of many non-contiguous elements. For example, the [[Financially Distressed Municipalities Act]] allows the commonwealth of [[Pennsylvania]] to merge contiguous municipalities to reduce [[financial distress]].

Geographic contiguity is important in [[biology]], especially [[range (biology)|animal ranges]]. For a particular species, its habitat may be a '[[contiguous range]]', or it might be broken, requiring periodic, typically seasonal migrations (see: [[Disjunct distribution]]). The same concept of contiguous range is true for human transportation studies in an attempt to understand census geography.<ref>[http://geodepot.statcan.ca/Diss/Reference/COGG/LongDescription_e.cfm?GEO_LEVEL=5&REFCODE=1&LANG=E Census Metropolitan Area, Statistics Canada] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051217115704/http://geodepot.statcan.ca/Diss/Reference/COGG/LongDescription_e.cfm?GEO_LEVEL=5&REFCODE=1&LANG=E |date=17 December 2005 }}</ref> It also comes into play with electoral geography and politics.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20061003184937/http://pan.oxfordjournals.org/cgi/content/abstract/10/3/217 The Electoral Geography of Weimar Germany: Exploratory Spatial Data Analyses of Protestant Support for the Nazi Party, by John O'Loughlin].</ref> In United States [[Real property#United States|real property]] and [[mineral rights]] law, touching of two tracts at a common corner (as [[Checkerboarding (land)|checkerboarded land]]) is generally considered ''contiguous.''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/contiguous|title=Contiguous|date=June 2021|publisher=Legal Information Institute ([[Cornell Law School]])|access-date=28 Dec 2021}}</ref>

[[File:Frankenstein's monster (Boris Karloff).jpg|thumb|[[Boris Karloff]] in [[James Whale]]'s 1931 film ''[[Frankenstein (1931 film)|Frankenstein]]'', based on [[Mary Shelley]]'s 1818 [[Frankenstein|novel]]. The monster is created by an unorthodox [[biology]] experiment.]]
[[Biology]] appears in fiction, especially but not only in [[science fiction]], both in the shape of real aspects of the science, used as themes or plot devices, and in the form of fictional elements, whether fictional extensions or applications of biological theory, or through the invention of [[Lists of fictional species|fictional organisms]]. Major aspects of biology found in fiction include [[evolution in fiction|evolution]], [[disease in fiction|disease]], [[genetics in fiction|genetics]], [[reproduction]] including [[parthenogenesis]], [[physiology]], [[parasitism in fiction|parasitism]] and [[symbiosis in fiction|symbiosis (mutualism)]], [[ethology]], and [[ecology]].

[[Speculative evolution]] enables authors with sufficient skill to create what the critic Helen N. Parker calls biological [[parable]]s, illuminating the human condition from an [[Extraterrestrial life|alien]] viewpoint. [[Extraterrestrials in fiction|Fictional alien animals and plants]], especially [[humanoid]]s, have frequently been created simply to provide entertaining monsters. Zoologists such as Sam Levin have argued that, driven by [[natural selection]] on other planets, aliens might indeed tend to resemble humans to some extent.

Major themes of science fiction include messages of optimism or pessimism; Helen N. Parker has noted that in biological fiction, pessimism is by far the dominant outlook. Early works such as [[H. G. Wells]]'s novels explored the grim consequences of Darwinian evolution, ruthless competition, and the dark side of human nature; [[Aldous Huxley]]'s ''[[Brave New World]]'' was similarly gloomy about the effects of [[genetic engineering]].

Fictional biology, too, has enabled major science fiction authors like [[Stanley Weinbaum]], [[Isaac Asimov]], [[John Brunner (novelist)|John Brunner]], and [[Ursula Le Guin]] to create what Parker called biological [[parable]]s, with convincing portrayals of alien worlds able to support deep analogies with Earth and humanity.

{{Short description|Sub-field of artificial intelligence}}
{{original research|date=January 2019}}
'''Argument technology''' is a sub-field of [[collective intelligence]] and [[artificial intelligence]] that focuses on applying computational techniques to the creation, identification, analysis, navigation, evaluation and visualisation of arguments and debates.

In the 1980s and 1990s, philosophical theories of [[argument]]s in general, and [[argumentation theory]] in particular, were leveraged to handle key computational challenges, such as modeling [[non-monotonic logic|non-monotonic]] and [[defeasible reasoning|defeasible]] reasoning and designing robust coordination protocols for [[multi-agent systems]].<ref>{{Citation|last1=van Eemeren|first1=Frans H.|chapter=Argumentation and Artificial Intelligence|date=2014|chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-90-481-9473-5_11|title=Handbook of Argumentation Theory|pages=615–675|editor-last=van Eemeren|editor-first=Frans H.|place=Dordrecht|publisher=Springer Netherlands|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-90-481-9473-5_11|isbn=978-90-481-9473-5|access-date=2021-12-08|last2=Garssen|first2=Bart|last3=Krabbe|first3=Erik C. W.|last4=Snoeck Henkemans|first4=A. Francisca|last5=Verheij|first5=Bart|last6=Wagemans|first6=Jean H. M.|editor2-last=Garssen|editor2-first=Bart|editor3-last=Krabbe|editor3-first=Erik C. W.|editor4-last=Snoeck Henkemans|editor4-first=A. Francisca|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref> At the same time, mechanisms for computing ''semantics'' of [[Argumentation framework]]s were introduced as a way of providing a calculus of opposition for computing what it is reasonable to believe in the context of conflicting arguments.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Prakken |first1=Henry |title=The ASPIC+ framework for structured argumentation: a tutorial |journal=Argument & Computation |date=2014 |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=31–62 |doi=10.1080/19462166.2013.869766 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

With these foundations in place, the area was kick-started by a workshop held in the Scottish Highlands in 2000, the result of which was a book coauthored by philosophers of argument, rhetoricians, legal scholars and AI researchers.<ref name="sac">Reed, C. & Norman, T.J. (eds) Argumentation Machines. Kluwer, 2003.</ref> Since then, the area has been supported by various dedicated events such as the International Workshop on Computational Models of Natural Argument (CMNA)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cmna.info |title=Computational Models of Natural Argument |website=www.cmna.info}}</ref> which has run annually since 2001; the International Workshop on Argument in Multi Agent Systems (ArgMAS) annually since 2004; the Workshop on Argument Mining,<ref>For example: {{cite web |url=https://www.aclweb.org/anthology/volumes/W19-45/ |title=Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Argument Mining – ACL Anthology |website=www.aclweb.org |publisher=[[Association for Computational Linguistics]] |date=August 2019 |access-date=7 December 2020}}</ref> annually since 2014, and the Conference on Computational Models of Argument (COMMA),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.comma-conf.org |title=Computational Models of Argument conference series |website=www.comma-conf.org}}</ref> biennially since 2006. Since 2010, the field has also had its own journal, ''Argument & Computation'', which was published by Taylor & Francis until 2016<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tandf.co.uk/journals/tarc |title=Journal of Argument & Computation |website=www.tandf.co.uk |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120221221912/http://www.tandf.co.uk/journals/tarc |archive-date=2012-02-21 }}</ref> and since then by IOS Press.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.iospress.nl/journal/argument-computation/ |title=Journal of Argument & Computation |website=www.iospress.nl|date=August 2023 }}</ref>

One of the challenges that argument technology faced was a lack of standardisation in the representation and underlying conception of argument in machine readable terms. Many different software tools for manual [[Argument map|argument analysis]], in particular, developed idiosyncratic and ad hoc ways of representing arguments which reflected differing underlying ways of conceiving of argumentative structure.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Scheuer |first1=O. |last2=Loll |first2=F. |last3=Pinkwart |first3=N. |last4=McLaren |first4=B.M. |title=Computer-supported argumentation: A review of the state of the art |journal=Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning |year=2010 |volume=5 |issue=1 |pages=43–102 |doi=10.1007/s11412-009-9080-x |s2cid=4473082 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220309167}}</ref> This lack of standardisation also meant that there was no interchange between tools or between research projects, and little re-use of data resources that were often expensive to create. To tackle this problem, the [[Argument Interchange Format]]<ref>{{Citation|last1=Rahwan|first1=Iyad|chapter=The Argument Interchange Format|date=2009|chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-98197-0_19|title=Argumentation in Artificial Intelligence|pages=383–402|editor-last=Simari|editor-first=Guillermo|place=Boston, MA|publisher=Springer US|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-0-387-98197-0_19|isbn=978-0-387-98197-0|access-date=2021-12-08|last2=Reed|first2=Chris|bibcode=2009aai..book..383R |hdl=21.11116/0000-0002-CA71-B |editor2-last=Rahwan|editor2-first=Iyad|hdl-access=free|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref> set out to establish a common standard that captured the minimal common features of argumentation which could then be extended in different settings.

Since about 2018, argument technology has been growing rapidly, with, for example, [[IBM]]'s Grand Challenge, [[Project Debater]], results for which were published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' in March 2021;<ref name="Slonim 379–384">{{Cite journal|last1=Slonim|first1=Noam|last2=Bilu|first2=Yonatan|last3=Alzate|first3=Carlos|last4=Bar-Haim|first4=Roy|last5=Bogin|first5=Ben|last6=Bonin|first6=Francesca|last7=Choshen|first7=Leshem|last8=Cohen-Karlik|first8=Edo|last9=Dankin|first9=Lena|last10=Edelstein|first10=Lilach|last11=Ein-Dor|first11=Liat|date=March 2021|title=An autonomous debating system|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-021-03215-w|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=591|issue=7850|pages=379–384|doi=10.1038/s41586-021-03215-w|pmid=33731946 |bibcode=2021Natur.591..379S |s2cid=232305184 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription}}</ref> German research funder, [[German Research Foundation|DFG]]'s nationwide research programme on Robust Argumentation Machines, RATIO,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Priority Programme "Robust Argumentation Machines (RATIO)" (SPP 1999/2)|url=https://www.dfg.de/en/research_funding/ai-initiative/priority_programme_1999_2/index.html|access-date=2021-12-08|website=www.dfg.de|language=en}}</ref> begun in 2019; and UK nationwide deployment of ''The Evidence Toolkit'' by the [[BBC]] in 2019.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Visser|first1=Jacky|last2=Lawrence|first2=John|last3=Reed|first3=Chris|date=2020-10-22|title=Reason-checking fake news|url=https://doi.org/10.1145/3397189|journal=Communications of the ACM|volume=63|issue=11|pages=38–40|doi=10.1145/3397189|s2cid=225041563 |issn=0001-0782|url-access=subscription}}</ref> A 2021 video narrated by [[Stephen Fry]] provides a summary of the societal motivations for work in argument technology.<ref>{{Citation|title=AI Exposes A Group Behind Covid, Brexit & Climate, w Stephen Fry.| date=2 October 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7cN3rZ5h3LE|language=en|access-date=2021-12-08}}</ref>

Argument technology has applications in a variety of domains, including [[education]], [[healthcare]], [[policy making]], [[political science]], [[intelligence analysis]] and [[risk management]] and has a variety of sub-fields, methodologies and technologies.<ref name="bex">{{cite book |editor1-last=Bex |editor1-first=Floris J. |editor2-last=Grasso |editor2-first=Floriana |editor3-last=Green |editor3-first=Nancy L. |editor4-last=Paglieri |editor4-first=Fabio |editor5-last=Reed |editor5-first=Chris |date=2017 |title=Argument Technologies: Theory, Analysis, and Applications |series=Studies in logic and argumentation |volume=68 |location=London |publisher=College Publications |isbn=9781848902183 |oclc=1012498399}}</ref>
